judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause bars contradiction by any other agreement "before the date hereof," which on its face leaves contemporaneous and later agreements untouched, and "reflects the entire understanding" is weaker than the usual "constitutes the entire agreement".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The "Loan Documents" definition includes "any other agreement entered into, now or in the future," so the integration clause expressly incorporates an open-ended and growing set of documents.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The appointment is called "irrevocable" and then made revocable by written notice in the same sentence, and the indemnity excludes only liability resulting "solely" from gross negligence or wilful misconduct — a narrow carve-out that is a familiar point of contest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Section's premise that the Loan Account and Collateral are handled "in a combined fashion" sits against Section 6.12's separateness covenants requiring each Borrower to keep its assets distinct from its Affiliates'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The form is riddled with unclosed brackets and blanks ("given to Lender]", "commencing on the first day of ,20"), so the operative election language cannot be read as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The bracketed instruction ("the first day of a month not less than 3 Business Days after the date of this Notice") does not match Section 2.12(c), which requires notice before the LIBOR Deadline, and the Dallas ZIP code differs from the one in Section 12.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Paragraph 6 certifies compliance with "Sections 7.16, and 7.37" — Section 7.37 does not exist — and paragraphs 2 and 5 make the same representation-bring-down twice with different exceptions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.3(a)(ii) and (c)(iii) require this certificate to demonstrate compliance with Sections 7.16 and 7.17, so the exhibit's cross-reference is wrong; Schedule 3 to the exhibit also repeats the impossible 0.9% Senior Leverage Ratio test.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Like its companion form, this exhibit contains unclosed brackets and blank dates, and the opening quotation mark for "LIBOR Rate Effective Date" is missing, so the notice cannot be completed from the text as printed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its "not less than 3 Business Days" instruction tracks Section 2.12(b), but Section 2.12(c)'s deemed-election rule makes an affirmative LIBOR Notice largely unnecessary — the form and the mechanism are out of step.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The account holder is given as "B-4 PARTNER, LLC," which is not the name of either Borrower, and the schedule supplies the definition of "Designated Account Bank" that Section 1.1 merely points to.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.12(d) forbids Borrowers from maintaining depository accounts other than Cash Management Accounts, and Section 2.6(a) requires all cash management at Wells Fargo after 60 days, yet this Designated Account is at Greater Bay Bank and Section 2.8 requires it be maintained.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short designation with a redacted account number; the substitution mechanism is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.3(a), 2.6(b) and 2.7.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Item 2 lists a future, contingent category ("Once a Permitted Reorganization is implemented, the Subordinated Liens securing Approved Debt") rather than an existing lien, so what is scheduled is indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1(b)(ii) refers to "any existing Permitted Lien set forth on Schedule P-1 which is specifically identified thereon as entitled to have priority over the Lender's Liens," but the schedule makes no such identification for either item.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two specific licences listed with numbers and dates; nothing ambiguous on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.3 represents that this schedule lists all licences required for "any Borrower" to conduct its business, yet the schedule lists nothing at all for B-4 Partners LLC, the Manager and Administrative Borrower.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short items identifying where Collateral is kept; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.5 and Section 6.9 both refer to it and Section 7.15's public-warehouse proviso contemplates a location the schedule does not list.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two lines plus a flat statement that there are no Subsidiaries.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The "SUBSIDIARIES - NONE" entry makes the whole "and its Subsidiaries" apparatus of Sections 5 through 7 inoperative at closing, and the Subsidiary definition's carve-outs make it likely to stay that way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single address; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the address in Sections 3.1(o) and 12 and Schedule 5.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The identification numbers are rendered as "Jo021" and "EEE0060," which cannot be actual organisational identification numbers as printed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.7(c) represents that these numbers are accurate and Section 7.5 forbids changing them, so an unreadable schedule undermines both.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One word; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 5.7(d) and Section 4.4(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long narrative that describes redemption rights as existing only "in the discretion of the Manager" while also reporting 50 pending redemption requests, and states that "all or substantially all" capital contributions have been made — a hedged factual assertion in a document meant to be a complete and accurate description.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.8(b) requires this schedule to be "complete and accurate" and excepts anything described "in an Offering Circular"; the redemption machinery it describes is what Section 7.10 and the Permitted Reorganization definition are built around, and Section 8.9(x) makes a default on capital obligations to members an Event of Default.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrative disclosure of two specific matters; the second sentence is loosely written but identifies the matter.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.10 carves out "actions to enforce Account Debtor obligations or Account Debtor bankruptcies," which appears to cover both disclosed matters anyway.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One word; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.16 nonetheless represents that Borrowers own or license all IP "necessary to the conduct of its business," and Section 4.4(c) imposes an elaborate patent, trademark and copyright registration regime — an apparatus with no subject matter.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short list of accounts with partially redacted numbers; definite in structure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Every listed account is at Greater Bay Bank, which cannot be squared with Section 2.6(a)'s requirement that Wells Fargo be the only Cash Management Bank 60 days after closing, nor with Section 6.12(d)'s prohibition on maintaining other depository accounts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short items with a cross-reference to Schedule 5.8; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.1(b) permits only "Indebtedness set forth on Schedule 5.20," so the single Fremont Bank loan is the entire permitted legacy debt; Schedule P-1 lists the same lien consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The two-column list has collapsed so that company names run into one another ("Commonwealth Land Title Insurance _ Company", "Land America Title Insurance Company -Ticor Title Insurance Company Co."), leaving it genuinely uncertain which entities are approved.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.21 represents this is "a true and complete list" and the "Approved Title Insurance Company" definition, the "Settlement Agent" definition and Eligible Notes Receivable clause (h) all depend on it.
